responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for Analog Devices Blackfin processors, covering the machine description, ABI, target options, and OS/subtarget variants needed to compile and link code for Blackfin systems. Its core files define Blackfin-specific machine modes, register and operand constraints, predicates, instruction-selection and scheduling patterns, including DSP-oriented and synchronization operations, while the backend implementation and headers provide the procedural target hooks for calling convention handling, frame layout, PIC/FDPIC and address legalization, prologue/epilogue generation, builtin expansion, hardware-loop support, assembler output, and target cost/legality decisions. The module also owns the Blackfin-specific -m option set and CPU/revision selection logic, plus ELF, Linux, uClinux, and RTEMS configuration overlays and multilib/sysroot support that adapt the generic Blackfin code generator to each runtime environment, making this directory the main locus of Blackfin code generation and target integration within GCC.
